title: Book 1 — Clio, Chapter 62
paragraphs: This oracle he uttered to him, being divinely inspired, and Peisistratus, understanding the oracle and declaring that he accepted the prophecy which had been spoken, led his army against the enemy. Now at that very moment the Athenians from the city happened to be occupied with the morning meal, and some of them after their meal with games of dice or with sleep. Then the forces of Peisistratus fell upon the Athenians and put them to flight. As they fled, Peisistratus devised a very skilful stratagem, so that the Athenians would not gather together again into one body but would remain scattered abroad. He mounted his sons on horseback and sent them before him, and overtaking the fugitives they said what Peisistratus had commanded: they bade the Athenians be of good cheer and that each man should depart to his own home.
